prose:
World 2030 presents a scenario in which cheaper digital goods have limited effect on household inflation because physical services dominate spending. The retrieved passage assigns explicit assumptions about the digital share of CPI, service inflation and interest-rate paths.

These are model premises and forecasts, not observed 2030 outcomes or an official central-bank projection. Only a short passage was readable, so the wider scenario construction, sensitivity analysis and evidential basis were not examined.
highlights: Digital-price effects depend on assumed spending weights
Physical service costs dominate its argument
Only a brief extract was available
